## bioRxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Google_Drive
This is an MCP server provided by Drive API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Drive.

- Do not change a refusal's text, its exit code or what it writes (nothing).
- Do not capture output other than the refusal sentence; do not capture a call whose `--session` is not the running session.

Before merge: close the pull request, delete the branch. After merge: `git revert <merge commit>` in a new pull request; the captured lines in committed scratchpads stay as records.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""scripts/audit/refusal_register.py — every writer refusal a batch met, and what became of each (T-088).

WHY THIS EXISTS. A writer's refusal is the only record of what the batch tried to hold and could not write
(a figure, an inadequacy statement), and it was printed once and lost: the session's command log keeps the
command and a hash of the output. `dbcore.record_refusal` now keeps each one in
`scratchpad/<session>/refusals.jsonl` (the file is committed with the session, CLAUDE.md rule 6). This script
reads that one file and records what became of each refusal, so a batch cannot be called done with a refusal
nobody answered (`/batch-done`).

    list [--session S]     each refusal with its disposition or UNDISPOSED; exit 1 if any is undisposed
    dispose --session S --ts T --as retried|parked|waived [--gap-id G] [--reason R]

A refusal line is `{ts, session, script, verb, argv, sentence, db}`; a disposition line is
`{kind: "disposition", refusal_ts, as, gap_id, reason, ts}` appended to the same file. A line without `kind`
is a refusal. `ts` has microseconds because `dispose` names a refusal by it and a retry loop refuses twice in
one minute. This script never writes the database, and it never writes a canonical row by hand (OD-54).

The dispositions are declared once, below, and read from there by both subcommands: a rule declared once in
a stated place (owner, 2026-11-12). What a disposition means:
  retried  the writer was right and the corrected call succeeded (not checkable here: say so in --reason if useful)
  parked   the content waits: a gap (`db.py add-gap`, typed by its subject) names what is held back and the
           refused argv in this file is the replay command; --gap-id is checked against the database the
           refusal names
  waived   nothing is held back, and --reason says why
"""
import argparse
import json
import re
import sqlite3
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
import dbcore  # noqa: E402  -- stdlib only

DISPOSITIONS = ("retried", "parked", "waived")


class Refused(Exception):
    """This script's own refusal: printed as `REFUSING: ...`, exit 1."""


def _session(given):
    """The bare stem of `given`, else of `scratchpad/CURRENT`; refused when neither names a folder."""
    stem = dbcore.session_stem(given) if given else None
    if not stem:
        cur = dbcore.REPO_ROOT / "scratchpad" / "CURRENT"
        stem = dbcore.session_stem(cur.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()) if cur.is_file() else None
    if not stem or "/" in stem:
        raise Refused("no session: give --session, or set scratchpad/CURRENT")
    return stem


def _read(stem):
    """(refusals, dispositions, unreadable) of the session's file: three lists of (line number, record). A file that
    does not exist is three empty lists, not an error. A line that is not a JSON object, or has an unknown `kind`,
    is unreadable and is reported, never skipped."""
    path = dbcore.REPO_ROOT / "scratchpad" / stem / "refusals.jsonl"
    refusals, dispositions, bad = [], [], []
    if not path.is_file():
        return refusals, dispositions, bad
    for n, raw in enumerate(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), 1):
        if not raw.strip():
            continue
        try:
            rec = json.loads(raw)
        except ValueError:
            rec = None
        if not isinstance(rec, dict):
            bad.append((n, "not a JSON object"))
        elif "kind" not in rec:
            refusals.append((n, rec))
        elif rec["kind"] == "disposition":
            if rec.get("as") in DISPOSITIONS:
                dispositions.append((n, rec))
            else:
                bad.append((n, f"unknown disposition {rec.get('as')!r}"))
        else:
            bad.append((n, f"unknown kind {rec['kind']!r}"))
    return refusals, dispositions, bad


def _one_line(text, width):
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", str(text)).strip()[:width]


def cmd_list(args):
    stem = _session(args.session)
    refusals, dispositions, bad = _read(stem)
    by_ts, problems = {}, [f"line {n}: unreadable ({why})" for n, why in bad]
    ts_held = [r.get("ts") for _, r in refusals]
    for n, d in dispositions:
        if d.get("refusal_ts") not in ts_held:
            problems.append(f"line {n}: a disposition for {d.get('refusal_ts')!r}, which no refusal of this file carries")
        elif d["refusal_ts"] in by_ts:
            problems.append(f"line {n}: {d['refusal_ts']!r} is disposed a second time")
        else:
            by_ts[d["refusal_ts"]] = d
    undisposed = 0
    if not refusals:
        print(f"no refusal captured for {stem}")
    for _, r in refusals:
        d = by_ts.get(r.get("ts"))
        if d is None:
            undisposed += 1
            state = "UNDISPOSED"
        else:
            state = f"{d['as']}" + (f" {d['gap_id']}" if d.get("gap_id") else "") + (f" ({_one_line(d['reason'], 80)})" if d.get("reason") else "")
        print(f"{r.get('ts')}  {r.get('verb')}  {_one_line(r.get('sentence'), 160)}  -> {state}")
    for p in problems:
        print(f"PROBLEM {p}")
    print(f"UNDISPOSED: {undisposed}")
    print(f"EXAMINED: {len(refusals)} refusal(s)")
    return 1 if undisposed or problems else 0


def _db_with_gaps(refusal):
    """The database the refusal names (`db`: a repository-relative or absolute path, `~` forms are not
    resolvable), else the one this process opens (GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH, else the canonical file)."""
    named = refusal.get("db")
    cand = [dbcore.REPO_ROOT / named] if named and not str(named).startswith("~") else []
    for p in cand + [dbcore.db_path()]:
        if p.is_file():
            return p
    raise Refused(f"neither the database the refusal names ({named!r}) nor {dbcore.db_path()} exists")


def cmd_dispose(args):
    stem = _session(args.session)
    refusals, dispositions, bad = _read(stem)
    held = [r for _, r in refusals if r.get("ts") == args.ts]
    if not held:
        raise Refused(f"no refusal of {stem} carries ts {args.ts!r}: `list` prints each refusal's ts")
    if len(held) > 1:
        raise Refused(f"ts {args.ts!r} is carried by {len(held)} refusal lines, so it cannot name one: edit the file by hand")
    if any(d.get("refusal_ts") == args.ts for _, d in dispositions):
        raise Refused(f"the refusal at {args.ts!r} is already disposed; a disposition is not rewritten here")
    reason = (args.reason or "").strip()
    if args.disposition == "parked":
        if not args.gap_id:
            raise Refused("parked needs --gap-id: file the gap first (`db.py add-gap`, typed by its subject), "
                          "the refused argv in this file is the replay command")
        db = _db_with_gaps(held[0])
        con = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db}?mode=ro", uri=True)
        try:
            row = con.execute("SELECT status FROM gaps WHERE gap_id = ?", (args.gap_id,)).fetchone()
        except sqlite3.Error as exc:
            raise Refused(f"{db} cannot answer for gap {args.gap_id!r}: {exc}")
        finally:
            con.close()
        if row is None:
            raise Refused(f"gap {args.gap_id!r} is not in the gaps table of {db}: parking needs a gap that holds the content")
        if not str(row[0]).startswith("OPEN"):
            raise Refused(f"gap {args.gap_id!r} is {row[0]!r}, not open: a closed gap holds nothing back")
    elif args.gap_id:
        raise Refused(f"--gap-id belongs to parked, not {args.disposition}")
    if args.disposition == "waived" and not reason:
        raise Refused("waived needs --reason: a refusal set aside without a reason is a refusal lost")
    line = {"kind": "disposition", "refusal_ts": args.ts, "as": args.disposition, "gap_id": args.gap_id or None,
            "reason": reason or None, "ts": datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f")}
    with open(dbcore.REPO_ROOT / "scratchpad" / stem / "refusals.jsonl", "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write(json.dumps(line, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    print(f"disposed {args.ts} as {args.disposition}" + (f" {args.gap_id}" if args.gap_id else ""))
    return 0


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    p = sub.add_parser("list", help="each refusal of a session and its disposition; exit 1 if any is undisposed")
    p.add_argument("--session", help="default: scratchpad/CURRENT")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_list)
    p = sub.add_parser("dispose", help="record what became of one refusal")
    p.add_argument("--session", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--ts", required=True, help="the refusal's ts, as `list` prints it")
    p.add_argument("--as", dest="disposition", required=True, choices=DISPOSITIONS)
    p.add_argument("--gap-id", help="parked: the open gap that holds the content")
    p.add_argument("--reason", help="waived: why; any other: optional")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_dispose)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        return args.fn(args)
    except Refused as exc:
        print(f"REFUSING: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

+def record_refusal(script, argv, sentence):
+    """Keep one writer refusal in `scratchpad/<running session>/refusals.jsonl`; never raises.
+
+    Called at every place a writer says no, before it exits, so the sentence (the only record of what the batch held
+    and could not write) outlives the terminal. The session's command log keeps a hash of the output, not the words.
+    Captured only when `--session` in `argv` IS the running session (`scratchpad/CURRENT`, whose folder must exist
+    under that exact name, CLAUDE.md section 7): a test or probe refusing under another session would otherwise fill
+    the batch's record with fixtures.
+
+    WHAT IS STORED, because the file is committed to a public repository (rule 6): `ts` (to the microsecond: two
+    refusals in one minute are one retry loop, and `refusal_register.py dispose` names a refusal by it), `session`,
+    `script`, `verb` (db.py's subcommand, else the script's own name), `argv` and `sentence` (the repository root
+    written relative, any home directory as `~`, the value after a flag named like a token, secret, password,
+    credential or api key replaced), and `db` (the `--db` value, else the database this process opens, scrubbed the
+    same way). Nothing else: no output, no environment, no user name. The stage, tables, rule ids and signature of a
+    refusal are derived by its reader from these fields, never stored (rule 8).
+    """
+    try:
+        argv = [str(a) for a in argv]
+        stem = (REPO_ROOT / "scratchpad" / "CURRENT").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
+        stem = session_stem(stem)
+        if not stem or "/" in stem:      # the folder must already exist under that exact name: the append below never creates it
+            return
+        given = _flag_value(argv, "--session", 5)
+        if given is None or session_stem(given) != stem:
+            return
+        clean, hide = [], False
+        for tok in argv:
+            name, eq, _ = tok.partition("=")
+            if hide:
+                clean.append("<redacted>")
+                hide = False
+            elif tok.startswith("--") and _SECRET_FLAG.search(name):
+                clean.append(f"{name}=<redacted>" if eq else tok)
+                hide = not eq
+            else:
+                clean.append(_scrub(tok))
+        line = {"ts": datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f"), "session": stem, "script": script,
+                "verb": argv[0] if script == "scripts/db.py" and argv else Path(script).stem,
+                "argv": clean, "sentence": _scrub(sentence),
+                "db": _scrub(_flag_value(argv, "--db", 4) or db_path())}
+        with open(REPO_ROOT / "scratchpad" / stem / "refusals.jsonl", "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:

@contextlib.contextmanager
def root88(current=S88, folder=S88):
    """A temporary tree with `scratchpad/CURRENT` (omitted when `current` is None) and a session folder (omitted when
    `folder` is None); `dbcore.REPO_ROOT` points at it inside the block."""
    base = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="t088-", dir=TMP))

    if folder:

    old, dbcore.REPO_ROOT = dbcore.REPO_ROOT, base

    return dbcore.record_refusal(script, argv, sentence)

    """Run `script`'s `__main__` in this process: (exit code or message, stdout, stderr). `dbcore.REPO_ROOT` is whatever the
    caller's `root88` set, so a refusal it keeps lands in the temporary tree."""
    out, err, old, code = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO(), sys.argv, None

    try:
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):

        code = exc.code

    return code, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()

    s = re.sub(r"-+", "-", s).strip("-")

def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split('\n\n')[0])
    p.add_argument("--session", help="Session filename, e.g. session_2026-05-11g-citation-mining.md")
    p.add_argument("--summary", help="One-line description for the frontmatter header")
    p.add_argument("--input", help="Read SQL from this path (default: stdin)")
    p.add_argument("--output-dir", default=str(MIGRATIONS_DIR))
    p.add_argument("--no-transaction", action="store_true",
                   help="Accepted no-op. Bodies are never wrapped: the migration "
                        "runner owns the transaction boundary (DR-2026-08-19 F5)")
    p.add_argument("--force-timestamp", help="Override timestamp (advanced; for tests only)")
    p.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true",
                   help="Run the range-guard mutation tests and exit (no --session/--summary needed)")
    args = p.parse_args()

    if args.selftest:
        sys.exit(selftest())

    if not args.session or not args.summary:
        p.error("the following arguments are required: --session, --summary")

    if args.input:
        with open(args.input) as f:
            sql = f.read()
    else:
        sql = sys.stdin.read()

    sql = sql.strip()
    if not sql:
        print("ERROR: empty SQL body", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    # Risky-pattern warnings
    warnings = []
    for pat, label in RISKY_PATTERNS:
        if pat.search(sql):
            warnings.append(label)
    if warnings:
        for w in warnings:
            print(f"  WARNING: detected risky pattern — {w}", file=sys.stderr)

    # Audit-enforced integer ranges — BLOCKING (see RANGE_GUARDS rationale).
    range_violations = check_range_guards(sql)
    if range_violations:
        print("  ERROR: value outside an audit-enforced range — migration NOT emitted.",
              file=sys.stderr)
        for col, val, lo, hi, enforced_by in range_violations:
            print(f"    {col}: {val} is not permitted. Allowed range: {lo}-{hi} inclusive.",
                  file=sys.stderr)
            print(f"      Enforced by {enforced_by}. SQLite has no CHECK on this column, so a "
                  f"bad value applies silently and only shows up as a lost integrity check.",
                  file=sys.stderr)
            print(f"      If the value is genuinely unknown, use NULL — not a placeholder "
                  f"integer.", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    if args.force_timestamp:
        ts = args.force_timestamp
    else:
        ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%d%H%M%S")
    slug = slugify_session(args.session)
    filename = f"data_{ts}_{slug}.sql"
    out_path = Path(args.output_dir) / filename

    # Retry on collision (extremely rare — same session emitting two migrations in same second)
    retries = 0
    while out_path.exists() and retries < 5:
        time.sleep(1)
        ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%d%H%M%S")
        filename = f"data_{ts}_{slug}.sql"
        out_path = Path(args.output_dir) / filename
        retries += 1
    if out_path.exists():
        print(f"ERROR: filename collision unresolvable after {retries} retries: {out_path}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    iso = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec='seconds')
    header = f"""-- {filename}
-- Data migration generated by scripts/emit_data_migration.py
-- Session:    {args.session}
-- Generated:  {iso}
-- Summary:    {args.summary}
--
-- This file is forward-only and immutable once committed. If a correction is
-- needed, emit a NEW data migration that compensates — do not edit this file.

"""
    # The runner owns the transaction boundary (DR-2026-08-19 §12.0, F5). A
    # wrapper here made executescript commit the body from inside the file, so
    # the body and its data_migrations ledger row committed separately and a
    # "rolled back" failure discarded only the ledger row. --no-transaction is
    # kept as an accepted no-op so existing invocations do not break.
    body = sql

    # A SECOND EMISSION OF THE SAME PAYLOAD IS A DOUBLE-APPLY, NOT A NEW MIGRATION.
    #
    # The only prior guard was the filename, and the collision handler above DEFEATS it:
    # on a clash it sleeps one second and picks a new timestamp, so re-running this
    # command produces `data_<t>_<slug>.sql` and `data_<t+1>_<slug>.sql` with byte-
    # identical bodies -- measured 2026-09-16, one second apart, payloads diff-empty.
    # `migrate_db.py` dedups by migration_id, which is derived from the filename, so it
    # sees two distinct migrations and applies BOTH: every INSERT in the batch lands
    # twice in canonical, and CLAUDE.md rule 3 makes that unfixable in place -- it takes
    # a compensating migration to undo.
    #
    # Nothing downstream catches it. `research_batch_dod.py` never reads the migrations
    # directory, and `migration_reproducibility` compares row COUNTS between canonical
    # and a rebuild -- a rebuild replays both files, so the doubled counts MATCH and the
    # blocking check passes green over a corpus inserted twice.
    #
    # So the refusal belongs here, at the only point that can still see both payloads.
    # It compares the SQL BODY and ignores the generated header, because the header
    # carries the timestamp that makes two identical emissions look different.
    prior = sorted(Path(args.output_dir).glob(f"data_*_{slug}.sql")) \
        if Path(args.output_dir).is_dir() else []
    for old_path in prior:
        try:
            old_text = old_path.read_text()
        except OSError:
            continue
        # Strip the leading generated comment block; everything after it is the payload.
        old_body = "".join(old_text.splitlines(keepends=True)[len(header.splitlines()):])
        if old_body.strip() == body.strip():
            print(f"ERROR: this payload is byte-identical to {old_path.name}, already "
                  f"emitted for session {args.session!r}. Emitting it again would apply "
                  f"the same batch twice: migrate_db.py keys on the filename, so it "
                  f"would treat both as distinct migrations and replay both. If this is "
                  f"a genuine re-emission after the first was discarded, delete the "
                  f"stale file; if you meant to correct an applied migration, rule 3 "
                  f"says emit a COMPENSATING migration, which will not be byte-identical "
                  f"to this one.", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(1)

    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out_path.write_text(header + body)
    print(str(out_path))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

definition.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
definition.description:
Withdraw a task suggestion you queued earlier with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion has gone stale: the issue was fixed in this session (by you or the user), it turned out not to be a problem after all, or you have queued a better-scoped replacement — in that case queue the replacement with spawn_task first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only a suggestion the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn. If they already started, dismissed or edited it, the result says so and nothing changes; that answer is final, so don't retry or re-flag it.

Read the result before you start the task anew or do it here: after "Not withdrawn", don't start it anew, and do it here only if the user asks for that in chat.

reason.description: Optional short note on why the suggestion is no longer needed, e.g. "fixed in this session" or "superseded by task_ab12cd34". It doesn't change the outcome.

task_id.description: The task_id from the spawn_task result that queued the suggestion (of the form task_1a2b3c4d).

definition.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
definition.description:
Suggest a separate task for something you noticed that is outside the scope of your current work.

Call this when you come across something that deserves fixing but doesn't belong in this change — dead code, stale docs, a missing test, a confirmed TODO, a bug or security issue spotted in passing. Don't use it for trivial fixes you can make inline, for anything the user asked you to do, for vague code-smell impressions or unverified hunches, or to split off parts of your own task. The call only queues a suggestion and returns; carry on with your current work.

The user sees a "Suggested task" card in the Claude desktop app with your title and tldr, can open the full prompt, and with one click starts it as a new session — on their machine in their local clone of this repository (optionally a fresh worktree of it), or in the cloud — sends it to this session, or dismisses it. A new session starts from your prompt alone, on a checkout that may not have this session's changes, so the prompt has to stand alone: what to change and why, the files involved by repository-relative path, and any context from this conversation it depends on. Absolute paths and other state of this environment may not exist there. If the find involves a secret or credential, say where it is rather than copying the value, since the prompt is stored and displayed.

The result carries a task_id; if the suggestion later becomes moot, withdraw it with dismiss_task.

prompt.description: The opening message of the new session: the goal, the files involved by repository-relative path, the context it needs from this conversation, and what done looks like. The user can read it in full before starting; markdown is fine. Keep it to what the task needs (hard limit 32000 characters) — the new session can read the code itself.

title.description: The card's heading and the new session's title: a short imperative phrase starting with a verb, under 60 characters, that makes sense on its own — e.g. "Fix stale README badge", "Remove dead config option".

tldr.description: One or two plain sentences on what the task would do and why it is worth doing. Shown on the card under the title; it is what the user reads when deciding whether to start it, so no file paths or code.

"""


def _refuse(sentence, code=1):
    """Say a refusal as `REFUSING: <sentence>` on stderr, keep it (T-088: `dbcore.record_refusal`) and exit `code`.
    Every place this engine says no goes through here, so none is left out of the batch's refusal record."""
    dbcore.record_refusal("scripts/assess/assess_cell.py", sys.argv[1:], sentence)
    print(f"REFUSING: {sentence}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(code)



def main():
    global SESSION, STAMP
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Determine one cell: a parameter under one or more lenses.",
        epilog="--db IS WRITTEN, NOT ONLY READ. The engine gathers the cell's evidence "
               "from it and INSERTs the determination -- plus any gap and convergence "
               "row -- straight back into it, committing before it exits. --emit-sql is "
               "a replayable COPY of those same inserts, not the only place they land: "
                    help="fixed timestamp, e.g. '2026-09-09 00:00:00'. An INPUT, never "
                         "now(): the engine run twice must be byte-identical.")
    ap.add_argument("--report-json", default=None)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if os.path.abspath(args.db) == os.path.abspath(os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "data", "guidebook.db")):
        _refuse("this engine never writes the canonical DB (owner-gated).")
    # The DB holds the bare session stem; the pointer form carries `.md` (CLAUDE.md section 7), and
    # a wrong form scopes a gate to nothing. A stamp is stored verbatim, so it is refused unless it
    # has the shape every live created_at has: dbcore.now() is 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM', and the engine's
    # own examples add seconds. Both refusals precede every write.
    if not re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}(:\d{2})?", args.stamp):

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # REFUSALS ARE MESSAGES, NOT STACK TRACES. The canonical-DB guard has exited cleanly
    # via sys.exit since this file was written, and every other refusal here — a merged
    # parameter, a lens code that is not live, a cell already determined — arrived as a
    # traceback with the sentence at the bottom. These messages cite the ruling and name
    # the next move; a stack trace above them buries the part the operator needs. Same
    # refusals, same non-zero exit, no stack. Refusal only: anything else keeps its
    # traceback, because anything else is a defect and its location is the evidence.
    try:

---
description: The gate that decides whether a research batch is actually finished
---

Never claim a batch is done from your own reading of it. Run the gate the
SessionStart contract names:

```
python3 scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"
python3 scripts/audit/adversarial_pass_audit.py --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"
python3 scripts/audit/search_log_completeness.py --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"
python3 scripts/audit/refusal_register.py list --session "$(cat scratchpad/CURRENT)"
```

The second line is RC4 (advisory): it FAILs if this session wrote to any of the 2026-08-19
RULE's research tables and no closed adversarial pass names it. That FAIL is not a reason to
close pass 1; LED-192 holds it open (`/adversarial` step 3). Run it on `CURRENT`, not via
`run_checks.py --all --battery research` — that battery's other session-scoped checks
(`research_dod_session`, `author_fidelity`, `citation_mining_session`) are still pointed
at `LATEST-RESEARCH`, which names the PREVIOUS session for the whole life of this one.

The third line is I5, also on `CURRENT`: it reads the WebSearch/WebFetch ledger the
harness hook wrote and FAILs a WebSearch query that no `search_executions.query_text` of
this session contains — a search you ran and did not log (R8). Log it with
`db.py log-search --backfill 1`: the row is a reconstruction, not a log made as the search
ran, and the `--prior-expectation` it still requires is written after the results, so it
is post hoc and must say so. Its REPORTED lines (unpersisted WebFetch URLs, bare curl/wget
hosts, and web rows logged with no web line on the ledger — a hook that may not have
fired) belong in the session record; they do not fail, and a NOTHING-IN-SCOPE verdict does
not clear them. It witnesses WebSearch and WebFetch only: a search run through an MCP tool
(Consensus, PubMed, Scholar Gateway) leaves no line, so a PASS says nothing about those. R8 still
owes each of them a `log-search` row, and `record_file` its result (DR-2026-09-26 §2.2b); the
gate can check neither.

The fourth line lists every writer refusal this batch met (each is kept in `scratchpad/<session>/refusals.jsonl`,
for a call made under the running session) and exits 1 while any is undisposed. Every writer refusal this batch met is disposed before the batch is done: **retried** (the writer was
right; the corrected call succeeded), **parked** (its content waits: file a gap with `db.py add-gap`, typed by its
subject, and keep the refused argv, which is the replay command), or **waived** (with a reason). Record each with
`refusal_register.py dispose --session S --ts T --as retried|parked|waived [--gap-id G] [--reason R]`. An undisposed
refusal is a batch that is not done.

**The session id is the bare stem in the DB and carries `.md` in pointer files.**
Wrong form scopes the gate to zero rows and every rule reports PASS over an empty
subject — green, and meaningless.

If it fails, the batch is not done. Fix the rows, re-emit, re-run. Do not
baseline the failure away: `governance/research-contract-baseline.json` ratchets
DOWN only, and raising a count there forgives fresh violations invisibly.

When it passes, confirm the corpus posture has not regressed:
scratchpad and transcripts (rule 6), open the PR last and unsubscribe_pr_activity at once (rule 9); research rows
and tooling ship in separate PRs (rule 10).

**When a writer refuses** (Layer 2 protocol; the capture is Layer 1, the `/batch-done` rule Layer 0): acknowledge (correct the call and write the row, if the refusal was right), or refuse-and-park (keep the refused argv, file a gap naming what is held back and go on: the batch is not held up), then replay (the parked content is written through the sanctioned writer in a later research PR, after the tooling PR that closes the gap has merged, rule 10). Never write the row by hand: the content waits in the refusal record, not in the database (`CLAUDE.md` rules 3 and 10; OD-54 is open). Every refusal a writer makes under the running `--session` is kept, its sentence and its argv, in `scratchpad/<session>/refusals.jsonl`; an argparse usage error never reaches a writer and is not kept. `python3 scripts/audit/refusal_register.py list` shows what the batch met and `dispose` records what became of each: retried (the corrected call succeeded), parked (with the gap's id) or waived (with a reason).

    skipped.append(tid)

def feature(tid, name, present, what):
    """Gate a round-2/3 case on a probe: absent, the case is red and names the feature."""
    if not present:

    return bool(present)




@contextlib.contextmanager
def scratch():
    """A second copy of the test database for a case that needs hand-built state (each such
    statement says HAND), with its own copy of the scratch retrieval log: a source minted on the copy
    takes an id the main copy will mint too, and the two must not hold each other's files. db.py follows
    GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH and GUIDEBOOK_RETRIEVAL_LOG at call time, so its writers act on the copies."""
    k = next(_scratches)
    path = os.path.join(TMP, f"scratch-{k}.db")
    shutil.copy(DB, path)
    root = os.path.join(TMP, f"scratch-log-{k}")
    os.makedirs(root)
    for e in pathlib.Path(retrieval_log.LOG_ROOT).iterdir():
        if e.is_symlink():
            os.symlink(os.readlink(e), os.path.join(root, e.name))
        elif e.is_dir():

    try:

    head, num = an_id.rsplit("-", 1)
